chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The free man and the free woman, when they commit adultery, every one of the two shall be flogged with one hundred lashes. So, as for the married man and the married woman, upon both of them is stoning.

key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: rajm — stoning to death; the hadd penalty for adultery committed by a married (muhsan) person
key_terms.الْحُرُّ: free man — a legally free person as opposed to a slave; the specification of free status is significant in classical Islamic law where slaves received half the hadd
key_terms.الْمُحْصَنُ: muhsan — a person in a valid, consummated marriage; subject to stoning (rajm) as the hadd for adultery
key_terms.جَلْدَة: jalda — a stroke or lash; the hadd of one hundred lashes for unmarried free persons who commit zina
key_terms.زَنَا: zina — unlawful sexual intercourse; the grave sin for which the hadd penalties are prescribed

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic punishment for adultery according to Imam al-Sadiq in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Sadiq's (AS) statement establishing the Islamic legal penalties for adultery (zina): one hundred lashes for unmarried free persons, and stoning (rajm) for those who are married (muhsan). The distinction between al-hurr/al-hurra (free persons, as opposed to slaves) and al-muhsan/al-muhsana (those in a valid marriage) reflects classical Islamic jurisprudence. This ruling aligns with Quran 24:2 on flogging for adultery while the stoning penalty for the muhsan derives from established prophetic tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Sama’at, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘The free man and the free woman, when they commit adultery, every one of the two would be whipped with one hundred lashes. So, as for the married man and the married woman, upon the both of them is the stoning’.
